title: Tinnitus with sound hyperacusis and reduced sound tolerance

patient.chiefConcern: Severe tinnitus with discomfort from everyday sounds

stages.title: 1. Extract the clinical story
stages.prompt: Which additional symptom should be characterized carefully?

options.text: Sound intolerance, situations that trigger discomfort, tinnitus impact and current sound-avoidance behaviours
Only whether the patient owns earplugs

stages.feedback: The case specifically combines tinnitus with hyperacusis/reduced sound tolerance, so both symptoms and avoidance behaviour matter.

stages.title: 2. Interpret the findings
stages.prompt: The case specifies mild SNHL with LDLs below 70 dB HL. What should the student recognize?

options.text: The presentation includes reduced sound tolerance that should be incorporated into individualized management
Low LDLs prove the patient should avoid all environmental sound
Mild SNHL makes sound intolerance irrelevant

stages.feedback: The specified low LDLs are part of the hyperacusis/reduced sound-tolerance presentation.

stages.title: 3. Check for red flags
stages.prompt: How should safety and sound exposure be approached?

options.text: Screen for relevant clinical red flags while avoiding unnecessary over-protection from ordinary safe sounds
Recommend continuous hearing protection in all environments
Skip assessment because the hearing loss is mild

stages.feedback: The protocol objective includes managing co-occurring hyperacusis/desensitization and avoiding over-protection.

stages.title: 4. Select management
stages.prompt: Which management direction best fits the case?

options.text: Provide education and individualized sound-tolerance management, with gradual desensitization when appropriate and attention to tinnitus needs
Advise complete avoidance of everyday sound
Fit amplification solely because tinnitus is present

stages.feedback: The case is designed around sound-tolerance management and desensitization rather than blanket sound avoidance.

stages.title: 5. Justify the decision

options.text: Tinnitus and reduced sound tolerance require an individualized plan that balances protection from hazardous sound with appropriate exposure to ordinary sound
All sound should be avoided to protect hearing
Hyperacusis should be ignored if pure-tone thresholds are only mildly reduced

stages.feedback: The learning objective is to avoid over-protection while addressing genuine sound discomfort.

stages.title: 6. Plan follow-up

options.text: Sound tolerance, tinnitus impact, avoidance behaviours, functional participation and patient-reported benefit

stages.feedback: Follow-up should capture both tinnitus impact and functional change in sound tolerance.
